Asdiscussed in [15], the Hamiltonian energy surface of a physical system is the sum of all conservative energy. That is, the Hamiltonian surface is the energy across all components which store, but do not dissipate energy. Such components do not in reality exist. However, real components can be separated into compo- nents for which this definition applies. For example, an inductor’s resistance dissipates energy, but its inductance stores energy. Therefore, the inductance is conservative and the resistance is nonconservative. The Hamiltonian energy surface is stable in the sense of Lyapunov if H(x) = 0, iff x=0 H(x) > 0, x = 0 .
